sources.title: Original interview note preserving the LeetCode 5 variant wording

claims.text: The source identifies a LeetCode 5 variant requiring a second-longest palindromic substring that is not a substring of the longest palindromic substring.
Tie, multiple-longest, no-solution, input-size and null/empty semantics are not preserved and are therefore explicitly separated from the source contract.

Under the explicitly declared leftmost-longest, strict-shorter, positional-containment contract, the candidate code matches an independent DP-table oracle on exhaustive ternary strings through length 9.

validation.command: extract candidate Solution.java; javac Solution.java ReviewerHarness.java && java ReviewerHarness
validation.reported_stdout: PASS candidate-vs-independent-dp-oracle alphabet-abc-length-0..9 unique-and-tied-longest no-solution null=rejected

boundary_tests.expected: candidate labels tie/multiple-longest/no-solution/size rules as clarification points, not source facts
no eligible strictly-shorter palindrome outside the longest anchor
declared leftmost-longest plus strict-shorter semantics are deterministic and explicitly non-source
candidate code matches DP-table oracle on all ternary strings through length 9

findings: The original repository note preserves only the LeetCode 5 variant statement and the non-containment rule; it does not preserve tie, multiple-longest, no-solution, null/empty or size semantics.
The candidate correctly separates those missing semantics from source facts and declares a deterministic reference contract instead of silently inventing them.

The candidate Java implementation is executed directly and matches a separately implemented dynamic-programming palindrome-table oracle on all ternary strings through length 9, including tied-longest and no-solution cases.
The explanation uses occurrence interval containment rather than conflating positional containment with string-value containment.
The project-experience section explicitly refuses to fabricate production experience for a pure algorithm question.
